text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The leaders of four Lithuanian oil companies think that the merger of the national oil concern Lietuvos Nafta could take no less than three to five months.
- The allocations from state budget for the salaries of public servants will increase by 350 million litas per year after Lithuanian lawmakers adopted a new salary law.

- The procedural section of the court case against 52 people accused of orchestrating the attack on the Vilnius TV tower on January 13, 1991 case started in Vilnius district court. The trial proper will start on November 5.

- Lithuanian Confederation of Industrialists of more than 1,300 enterprises and which was considered to be a supporter of ruling Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party, has formed a long-term term economic alliance with the Homeland Union. It in in turn promised to allocate to industry no less than 50 percent of foreign credits taken in the state's name and to discuss with industrialists the candidates to the next cabinet of ministers.
- The government suggested a quota of 2,250 immigrants to Lithuania in 1997.
- The director of the German Economic Eastern Commission said that privatisation in Lithuania was not carried out successfully enough to attract foreign investors.

- The government approved a finance ministry suggestion to calculate the volume of foreign loans from the revenues of the national budget. Foreign loans as a percentage of the budget were 23.26 percent and calculating from the revenues of the national budget were 16.01 percent on September 1. According to the law, foreign loans cannot exceed 20 percent of GDP and constituted 13.7 percent on September 1 in Lithuania.
- The economy ministry forecasts that investments from various sources will show an annual 7.2 percent growth in 1997-1999.
- The newspaper has an interview with former Soviet intelligence officer Ricardas Vaigauskas about his business activities in Lithuania.
